async148b.baseline_note: Main sink at base commit; identical checkpoint profiling. Main control omits only the zero-timeout line from the candidate checkpoint helper, retaining its existing five-second wait.
async148b.probe_note: WAL bytes are allocated file size immediately before/after EndRun checkpoint, not peak sampling; frames are [busy, log frames, backfilled frames] from NOOP; result is the same tuple from TRUNCATE.
async148b.mechanism: Blocking EndRun TRUNCATE checkpoint exhausted its busy timeout and returned busy with partially backfilled WAL; precise blocker identity remains unproven.
async148b.repair: Temporarily zero busy timeout for best-effort EndRun TRUNCATE; restore prior timeout even when the pragma errors. COMMIT, synchronous modes, reference durability, autocheckpoint hook and shutdown checkpoint are unchanged.
async148b.decision_reason: Real-C faster in all three final pairs, but lab median 16.2 percent slower and two lab pairs regress; keep criterion is not met. Pinned WAL frames remain a risk.
